Justice CM Poonacha has sought a response from the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the Karnataka Department of Health and Family Welfare, and the Food Safety and Drug Administration in Karnataka. Justice CM Poonacha The petitioners have challenged an October 1 circular issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration in Karnataka. items.title: SC Collegium recommends 9 lawyers for appointment as J&K and Ladakh High Court judges; drops former AG's name
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of nine lawyers, including a woman, as judges of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The decision was taken during the Collegium meeting held on October 29, Thursday. As per the Collegium statement published on the Supreme Court website, the persons recommended for appointment are: - Vishal Sharma; - Vikram Kumar Sharma; - Namgyal Wangchuk; - Pawan Kumar Kundal; - Tahir Majid Shamsi; - Tabasum Zafar; - Amit Gupta; - Pranav Kohli; - Anupam Raina. Among the nine, advocates Namgyal Wangchuk hails from Ladakh, giving representation to the Union Territory in the proposed judicial appointments. The inclusion of advocate Tabasum Zafar is also noteworthy. If her appointment is formally cleared, she would become the first Kashmiri woman lawyer to be appointed as a judge of the High Court. The High Court Collegium , headed by the then Chief Justice Arun Palli, had recommended eleven names in April 2026, comprising ten advocates under the Bar quota and one judicial officer under the bench quota. In a first, Kashmiri woman lawyer among 11 recommended by Collegium for elevation to J&K HC However, the Supreme Court Collegium has now approved only nine out of the ten advocates recommended under the Bar quota. The name of Senior Advocate Jahangir Iqbal Ganai, former Advocate General of Jammu & Kashmir (June 2016–July 2018), does not figure in the approved list. The Collegium has not disclosed any reason for not approving his name. The judicial officer recommended by the High Court Collegium under the Bench quota, Yash Paul Bourney, had separately received the Supreme Court Collegium’s approval on September 10 and his appointment was notified by the Union Government on September 19. The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh has a sanctioned strength of 25 Judges, comprising 19 permanent and six additional Judges. The High Court currently has 14 working judges, leaving 11 vacancies. The nine proposed appointments would constitute a substantial step towards filling the vacancies. [Read Collegium Statement]

items.title: Cyclone Arnab impact on Andhra: Seven dead, CM Naidu estimates Rs 4600 crore loss
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu visited cyclone-affected areas in the state in the aftermath of Cyclone Arnab, which made landfall along the state’s coast on October 28. The Chief Minister said that at least seven people were killed in the cyclone. A preliminary estimate puts the losses caused by the cyclone at Rs 4,600 crore, he said, adding that the figure could increase after a detailed assessment. On October 29, CM Naidu carried out an aerial survey over cyclone-affected areas in the Dr BR Ambedkar Konaseema district. He inspected the relief centres at Gachakayalapora village in Mummidivaram constituency and interacted with cyclone victims. Addressing the media, the CM announced that Central teams would visit the state on October 30 to assess the cyclone damage. He said that he spoke to Union Home Minister Amit Shah about the cyclone situation and the measures taken by the state government, and submitted a preliminary damage report to the Union government. Naidu announced that a compensation of Rs 1,500 will be provided for each damaged coconut tree and each damaged oil palm tree. Families returning from relief camps will be given 25 kg of rice, a packet of essential commodities and financial assistance for their immediate expenses. Farmers will receive compensation if their yields decline due to the cyclone, he said. Extensive crop damage has been reported in 16 districts, with West Godavari, Kakinada, East Godavari, Konaseema and Krishna districts being affected the most. Dr BR Ambedkar Konaseema and West Godavari districts have been worst affected by the cyclone. Around 8,000 electricity poles fell in Konaseema district alone. Andhra Pradesh has requested the Telangana government to send 1,000 electricity department personnel to assist with restoration work. The rainfall received between October 26 and 29 is estimated to have brought approximately 380 tmc of water to the state. Meanwhile, former CM and YSRCP chief YS Jagan Mohan Reddy alleged that the TDP-led government had failed to provide timely relief to farmers. He questioned how crop losses were being assessed remotely without officials visiting fields. He alleged that the government’s crop loss figures kept changing, while power restoration and field-level assessment remained incomplete.

items.title: Hyderabad water board launches PAANI app for citizens to report water wastage
items.summary: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) on Thursday, October 30, launched a mobile application called PAANI (Water Warriors) to encourage citizens to report drinking water wastage and misuse, as the city braces for a possible water shortage of up to 100 million gallons a day (MGD) between January and August 2027. Launching the app at the HMWSSB headquarters in Khairatabad, Transport and BC Welfare Minister Ponnam Prabhakar urged households to reduce their water consumption by at least 20%. He cited concerns over possible rainfall deficits due to El Niño conditions and called for greater public participation in conserving water. Earlier this month, restaurants and pubs such as Paradise in Secunderabad, and Forefathers and Anaganaga in Jubilee Hills, were fined Rs 20,000 each by the water board for allegedly misusing water. The PAANI app will allow registered citizens to report instances of drinking water wastage and misuse in their neighbourhoods. Residents can register as 'Save Water Volunteers' through the HMWSSB website by submitting a government-issued identity document. Once their details are verified, they can use the app, available on the Google Play Store, to report violations. Complaints submitted through the app will undergo SMS-based verification, followed by field inspections by officials. The identities of volunteers reporting violations will be kept confidential. If water misuse is confirmed, notices will be issued to the individuals or organisations concerned, and penalties imposed in accordance with the rules. The Minister said that the primary objective was to build public awareness and encourage responsible water consumption rather than merely impose fines. The government will also recognise volunteers who make significant contributions to water conservation, with the Chief Minister expected to personally meet and commend “outstanding volunteers”. The launch comes amid concerns over Hyderabad's drinking water supply. HMWSSB Managing Director K Ashok Reddy said the board currently supplies around 560-570 MGD to the city but expects a shortfall of approximately 100 MGD from the Singur and Manjeera reservoirs between January and August 2027. The board is working to mobilise an additional 60 MGD from the Godavari and Krishna rivers and Osmansagar reservoir. items.summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has extended the deadline for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Delhi, Haryana, and Nagaland. For both Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, the date for publication of the final electoral rolls has been pushed from to November 30, from November 9 and October 30 respectively. The poll panel communicated the revised schedules to the respective Chief Electoral Officers following requests from them. PHOTO | ECI has extended the timeline for special intensive revision of electoral rolls in six states and Union Territories. The schedules were revised for Nagaland, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Maharashtra and Delhi. pic.twitter.com/XrzDcPWUs5 — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) October 29, 2026 As per the revised schedule announced on October 29, the notice phase and disposal of claims and objections will now conclude on November 26 for Telangana, instead of the earlier deadline of November 5. For Andhra Pradesh, this date has been extended to November 20. Telangana Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) C Sudharsan Reddy wrote to the ECI on October 29 seeking an extension of the schedule. In Telangana, the SIR exercise began with 3,38,26,448 registered voters. Of these, 2,64,87,213 submitted their enumeration forms. The remaining 73,39,235 electors were categorised under Absent, Shifted, Death and Duplicate (ASDD) entries and excluded from the draft electoral rolls. In Andhra Pradesh, out of nearly 4.16 crore voters who were on the pre-SIR rolls, enumeration forms were collected from 3.71 crore, or 89.22% of them, who made it to the draft roll. Around 44.89 lakh names were removed as they were found absent, shifted, dead/deleted or duplicate (ASDD). In Telangana, as of October 29, 92,81,189 of the 92,88,188 notices generated under the SIR exercise in Telangana had been delivered to voters according to the CEO’s office, leaving only 6,999 notices pending. Hearings have been completed for 92,08,443 notices. Meanwhile, 78,108 first hearings and 1,636 rescheduled hearings had lapsed as of October 29. A total of 2,59,22,684 voters had been cleared for inclusion in the final electoral rolls. This includes 59,31,395 electors who had cleared logical discrepancy checks and 30,64,168 unmapped electors identified through the 2002 SIR records. items.title: After Theni jailbreak, Tamil Nadu DGP Prisons Sandeep Rai Rathore transferred
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has transferred Director General of Police (Prisons) Sandeep Rai Rathore, two days after 17 undertrial prisoners escaped from the Thekkampatti sub-jail in Theni district in a major security breach. All 17 prisoners have since been apprehended following a 43-hour search operation. Rathore has now been posted as Director General of Police and Chief Vigilance Officer at TANGEDCO in Chennai. K Shankar, Additional Director General of Police (ADGP), Enforcement Bureau-CID, has been appointed as the new ADGP of Prisons and Correctional Services, according to a government order signed by Principal Secretary A Karthik on Thursday, October 29. Shankar, who is due for elevation to the rank of DGP in January 2027, has previously served in the prisons department as ADGP. Rathore's transfer came a day after police arrested the final two fugitives, identified as Tirupathi and Meenakshisundaram, bringing the search operation to an end. The jailbreak took place around 10 pm on Monday, October 26, when the inmates allegedly staged a fake medical emergency to overpower prison staff. One of the prisoners pretended to suffer an epileptic seizure, prompting a guard to enter their cell to assist him. The inmates then allegedly assaulted the guard, seized the keys to the main gate and escaped towards nearby forest areas. During their escape, the prisoners reportedly travelled on a motorcycle from Aranjanaipudur towards Uthamapalayam. They later borrowed a mobile phone from a stranger in Ammachipuram to contact their associates, who allegedly arranged money, clothes and vehicles for them. The search operation involved 17 specialised police teams, five Special Task Force units and four Tamil Nadu Special Police battalions. Drones were also deployed to scan the dense forest areas where the fugitives were suspected to be hiding. Following their recapture, the prisoners are being shifted to high-security correctional facilities across the state. Five of them were produced before a judicial magistrate on October 27 and remanded to judicial custody until November 10. Another eight were produced in court on October 28 and remanded until November 11. The remaining prisoners were also produced before the court on October 29. After completing the legal formalities, the inmates will be transferred to central prisons in Salem, Vellore, Cuddalore and Puzhal.
